newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Unibanco prices Eurobond at record tight spread.
newsitem.headline: Unibanco prices Eurobond at record tight spread.

text.p: Brazilian retail bank Unibanco priced a $150 million three-year Eurobond Wednesday at a record low spread of 190 basis points over U.S. Treasuries and had little trouble placing the issue, traders said.
"When you look at it coming in at 190 over, it seems shocking. But there was a lot of demand for it," said a trader at one of the banks that co-managed the deal.
He said much of the demand came from European investors, who would probably hold the paper to maturity.

Brazil debt watchers noted that the deal priced an even 100 bps below Unibanco's $100 million three-year bond issued in July 1996, reflecting a strong tightening in Brazilian paper over the past six months.
Spreads on many top-name Brazilian Eurobonds have been tightented even further recently on strong enthusiasm for high-yielding emerging market paper.
Brazilian banks Bradesco and Safra launched similar deals over the past two weeks at record low spreads. There is growing market talk that Brazilian Banco Itau will join them soon.
